prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a temple standing today that Russell M. Nelson dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where Russell M. Nelson dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church from 2018 to 2025, dedicated the Rome Italy Temple in 2019, the first temple in Italy. He also dedicated Sapporo Japan (2016) and Concepción Chile (2018) and rededicated Nuku'alofa Tonga (2007). Later he rededicated Washington D.C. (2022) and Manti Utah (2024).

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Manti Utah (rededicated 2024); Washington D.C. (rededicated 2022); Deseret Peak Utah (2024); and others.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Rome Italy (2019).

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: Concepción Chile (2018).

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Sapporo Japan (2016).

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Nuku'alofa Tonga (rededicated 2007).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose first temple was announced in 2019 or 2020.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country or territory whose first temple was announced in 2019 or 2020.
prompts.note: Hong Kong, which has had a temple since 1996, is counted separately from mainland China.
prompts.summary: In 2019 and 2020 eight countries and territories got their first temple announcement, including Hungary, Sierra Leone, Papua New Guinea, Kiribati and China (Shanghai). As of October 2026 none of the eight is dedicated yet; most are under construction.

answers.name: People's Republic of China
answers.fact: Shanghai, announced 2020.

answers.name: United Arab Emirates
answers.fact: Dubai United Arab Emirates, announced 2020.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: Budapest Hungary, announced 2019.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Pago Pago American Samoa, announced 2019.

answers.name: Kiribati
answers.fact: Tarawa Kiribati, announced 2020.

answers.name: Papua New Guinea
answers.fact: Port Moresby Papua New Guinea, announced 2019.

answers.name: Sierra Leone
answers.fact: Freetown Sierra Leone, announced 2019.

answers.name: Vanuatu
answers.fact: Port Vila Vanuatu, announced 2020.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place where the New Testament records people being baptized
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place where the New Testament records people being baptized
prompts.note: The lower Jordan runs between Jordan and the West Bank, so both count; Israel counts through Jerusalem and Caesarea.
prompts.summary: Baptism follows the gospel across the map. John baptized at the Jordan and in Bethabara beyond it. Three thousand were baptized at Jerusalem on Pentecost, Philip baptized in Samaria, and Saul was baptized in Damascus. Gentiles followed at Caesarea, then Lydia and a jailer at Philippi, many at Corinth, and twelve disciples at Ephesus.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: About three thousand were baptized at Jerusalem on Pentecost, and Cornelius' household at Caesarea (Acts 2:41; 10:48).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: John baptized in Bethabara beyond Jordan, on the river's east side; BD Bethabara says the exact site is unknown, but scripture puts it beyond the river (John 1:28; 10:40).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Philip baptized men and women in the city of Samaria; John preached in the wilderness of Judea by the Jordan (Acts 8:12; Matthew 3:1-6).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Lydia and the jailer were baptized at Philippi, and many Corinthians at Corinth (Acts 16:15, 33; 18:8).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Saul arose and was baptized in Damascus after Ananias restored his sight (Acts 9:17-18).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: About twelve disciples at Ephesus were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus (Acts 19:1-7).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place or people named in the book of Ezra, from Cyrus's Persia to Joppa
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place or people named in the book of Ezra: Cyrus king of Persia, the captives in Babylon, cedar from Lebanon floated to Joppa, the adversaries in Samaria, the roll found at Achmetha in Media, and the peoples Ezra warned against marrying (including Hittites, Ammonites, Moabites and Egyptians)
prompts.note: Samaria is in the West Bank (Palestine); Joppa (Jaffa) is in Israel. Jerusalem is scored as Israel, as in the other Bible prompts.
prompts.summary: Cyrus of Persia let the Jews in Babylon return and rebuild the temple. They paid Zidon and Tyre for cedar from Lebanon, shipped to Joppa, and pressed on despite adversaries who wrote from Samaria to the Persian king. Darius found Cyrus's decree at Achmetha and the temple was finished; later Ezra came to teach the law (Ezra 1-10).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Cyrus king of Persia proclaimed the return, and his decree was found at Achmetha in the province of the Medes (Ezra 1:1-2; 6:2); the Elamites were among Samaria's settlers who wrote against the Jews (Ezra 4:9).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: The captives went up from Babylon unto Jerusalem (Ezra 1:11).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: They rebuilt the house of God at Jerusalem, and cedar was brought by sea to Joppa (Ezra 3:7-8).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Meat, drink and oil went to them of Zidon and Tyre for cedar trees from Lebanon (Ezra 3:7).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Egyptians are also in Ezra's list of peoples whose abominations Israel had joined (Ezra 9:1).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Ezra mourned that the people had mingled with Ammonites and Moabites (Ezra 9:1).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: The adversaries wrote to Artaxerxes, and his answer went to Rehum and those dwelling in Samaria (Ezra 4:17).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Ezra 9:1 names the Hittites among the peoples Israel had mingled with; the Bible Dictionary places the Hittite nations north of Palestine from the Orontes to the Euphrates, with an empire reaching into Asia Minor.

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Ezra 9:1 names the Hittites among the peoples Israel had mingled with; the Bible Dictionary places the Hittite nations north of Palestine from the Orontes to the Euphrates, with an empire reaching into Asia Minor.

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country whose Global Histories chronology records its missionaries leaving when World War I began in 1914.
prompts.text_original: When World War I broke out in 1914, Church leaders released the missionaries serving in continental Europe but left those in Great Britain in place. Pin a European country whose Church Global Histories chronology records its missionaries leaving or being evacuated when the war began.
prompts.citation: Saints vol. 3 ch. 11; Global Histories chronologies
prompts.note: Great Britain does not count: its missionaries stayed. Norway does not either: its chronology records only that fewer were sent.
prompts.summary: At the start of World War I, the First Presidency told European leaders to release German and French missionaries, and mission president Hyrum M. Smith then pulled missionaries out of the rest of continental Europe. Missionaries in Great Britain stayed. Local Saints across the continent led branches and preached on their own until the war ended.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: All North American missionaries left Germany during World War I; local members were called to preach (GH Germany, 1914-1919).

answers.name: France
answers.fact: All missionaries left; the French Mission was absorbed, August 1914.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: Full-time missionaries were evacuated from Belgium during the war (GH Belgium, 1914-18).

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: All missionaries evacuated, August 1914.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Mission president told to release all missionaries, August 30, 1914.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Missionaries not native to Denmark sent home, October 1914.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: Missionaries serving in the Netherlands were reassigned to safer missions (GH Netherlands, 1914-19).

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Missionaries from the United States left Sweden in October 1914; local Saints took over the branches.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: All missionaries evacuated, August 10, 1914.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: Missionary work discontinued in 1914.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: Last missionary in Brasso (Brasov) left after the war began.
